articles.title: Princess’s gambit: At 11, Bodhana Sivanandan is an international master
articles.summary: LONDON: Bodhana Sivanandan, an 11-year-old BritishIndian chess prodigy of Tamil origin, has added another string to her bow by becoming the youngest
articles.body: LONDON: Bodhana Sivanandan, an 11-year-old BritishIndian chess prodigy of Tamil origin, has added another string to her bow by becoming the youngest female chess player to qualify for the International Master (IM) title.Sivanandan, who lives in the London suburb of Harrow, broke the 38-year-old record held by Hungarian chess legend Judit Polgar, widely regarded as the greatest female player in chess history, after winning her final-round game at the European Women’s Club Cup in Budva, Montenegro on Friday.Sivanandan secured her third and final IM norm at the tournament and crossed the required live rating threshold of 2400, completing the conditions for the IM title, the secondhighest open title in chess.‘Bodhana is a generational talent’Polgar had qualified at the age of 12 in 1988 and went on to become a top-10 player in the world, famously competing against the very best male grandmasters.Bodhana Sivanandan recovered from an opening-round defeat against former Women’s World Championship challenger GM Aleksandra Goryachkina to finish with 5.5 points from seven games. Her final-round win over Sweden’s WIM Viktoria Johansson in 32 moves contributed to a 4-0 victory for her team, She Plays To Win Lionesses A, and placed her among the 10 youngest players ever to qualify for the IM title.Last month, she became the youngest player in history to fulfil the requirements for the Woman Grandmaster (WGM) title.GM Mert Erdogdu, who has coached Sivanandan since Jan 2026, told Chess.com, “Her progress was inevitable, as she loves the game and works very hard. I work with her four times a week.”“You can only describe her as a generational talent, I am delighted that it’s happening,” IM Malcolm Pein, director of international chess and external relations at the English Chess Federation, told Chess.com.You use AI every day. articles.title: In 1997, after his ex-girlfriend’s cancer diagnosis, New Mexico’s Ra Paulette carved her a cave home; she lived there for 15 years among skylights and stone beds
articles.summary: Discover the remarkable story of Ra Paulette, the artist who, in 1997, created a stunning underground cave home for his former girlfriend, Liz Neymark, after her devastating cancer diagnosis. Explore the intricate details of this artistic endeavor and its impact on their lives.
articles.body: Artist Ra Paulette was known for carving underground spaces in New Mexico’s sandstone. He began work on a cave home for Liz Neymark, who was diagnosed with advanced melanoma and breast cancer, and her husband, Shel, in 1997. The finished project included skylights, built-in seating, carved bed platforms, and electricity and running water, according to ABC News’s 2015 report.Paulette had once been in a relationship with Liz, but she was married to Shel Neymark by the time the project began. Paulette intended to make the cave a residence, unlike many of his other excavations, which were designed as artistic or contemplative spaces. By 2015, the Neymarks had reportedly lived there for 15 years.Two years of digging and carvingPaulette had to remove sandstone and shape the interior as he went, and worked entirely by hand with tools which included a pick, wheelbarrow and brushes. He had to put in constant physical effort, with a 2015 profile in DuJour reporting that he spent more than two years on the Neymarks’ cave and worked about 20 hours a week.Paulette excavated rooms and features directly into the sandstone, and shaped the walls, openings and furnishings as part of the structure. He built skylights which brought daylight underground, while built-in platforms acted as beds and seating. A striking feature of the living room was that a circular section was carved into the floor that produced a drumming sound when someone danced on it, ABC News reported. The practical amenities included electricity and running water, and the bathroom featured a sunken tub. Shel Neymark contributed tilework to the interior, according to ABC News.A home that was built during a serious illnessDuJour reported that doctors had given Liz a 20% chance of living five years, and the article described Paulette’s work as a personal act of devotion. Liz was still alive in 2015, 18 years after the diagnosis, when ABC News published its report, and the cave had by then been occupied by the Neymarks for about 15 years. A 2014 CBS News profile of Paulette described him spending decades digging caves, often alone with his dog, and treating the process as a form of sculptural work.CaveDigger is a short documentary directed by Jeffrey Karoff that documented Paulette’s cave projects. It was released in 2013 and followed Paulette’s work in northern New Mexico and examined disagreements that came up when clients wanted different results or timelines from the artist. It was nominated for an Academy Award for Best Documentary Short at the 2014 Oscars, with the American Film Institute’s film synopsis describing how Paulette eventually set aside commissioned work to work on a large project that he expected to take a decade.Part of a larger body of underground workSome of Paulette’s other projects included spaces that were meant to be wilderness shrines, with curved walls, sculpted chambers and openings that brought sunlight into the rock. He used labor-intensive and unconventional methods, and described breaking the digging process into movements and patterns that made the work more manageable.The Neymarks’ cave was designed for daily life, since its sleeping areas, bathroom, seating and utilities were incorporated into the excavated stone, and also made it different from caves that were intended primarily for visitors or meditation. Paulette continued working on other caves after the home was completed, and by the time of the 2015 ABC News report, he had spent years developing a project called Luminous Caves, which is a larger complex that was designed to use sunlight entering through tunnels and openings in the rock. The Neymarks’ home remained one of his few excavations built specifically to function as a private residence.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: An Illinois mansion had $8.75 million in insurance coverage after a fire, but its owner received just $25,000 for most contents used in a wedding and lodging business
articles.summary: A lightning strike destroyed Pine Manor, a 24,000-square-foot mansion in southern Illinois, in October 2019, leaving owner Wesley Gibson facing a dispute
articles.body: A lightning strike destroyed Pine Manor, a 24,000-square-foot mansion in southern Illinois, in October 2019, leaving owner Wesley Gibson facing a dispute over insurance coverage for the antiques, artwork and furnishings inside. His homeowner’s policy with Chubb National Insurance Company covered the building for $8.75 million and its contents for $3.5 million. Chubb paid the full amount for the house but limited the contents payout to $25,000, arguing that most of the property had been used to operate a commercial lodging and events venue. Gibson challenged the decision, saying the policy should cover his collection of personal belongings. On July 13, 2026, the US Court of Appeals for the Seventh Circuit upheld the insurer’s position in Gibson v. Chubb National Insurance Company. The court concluded that most of the mansion’s contents were used to conduct Gibson’s business and fell under the policy’s business-property limit. The ruling turned on the policy’s wording and how the contents were used, rather than when or why they had been acquired.How Pine Manor became a wedding venue and luxury lodging businessGibson bought Pine Manor in the late 1990s as a vacation home for his family. Located on a private lake in the foothills of the Shawnee National Forest near Carbondale, Illinois, the 24,000-square-foot mansion was gradually transformed into a commercial lodging and events complex. Gibson spent millions renovating the property and furnishing it with family heirlooms, artwork and antiques, including an Italian rococo-style mirror and windows from the original Lloyd’s of London building. The estate eventually expanded to almost a dozen structures across more than 100 wooded acres. Its amenities included conference facilities, a pool, a carriage house, a boat dock and sports courts. Gibson also acquired neighbouring properties to accommodate additional guests and marketed Pine Manor as a luxury country inn and resort.The business generated substantial income. Between 2016 and 2019, Gibson’s consulting firm paid a $70,000 monthly retainer to use the estate for corporate training retreats, which could occupy up to 20 weeks each year. Pine Manor also hosted between 6 and 16 weddings annually, according to the court’s opinion. In both 2017 and 2018, the estate earned about $1 million in lodging revenue. Gibson’s tax returns reported 365 fair-rental days. Although Gibson and his family continued to stay at Pine Manor for about 70 nights a year, the property’s primary use had shifted to commercial accommodation and events. The estate held the relevant licences for its operations, and Gibson employed an on-site property manager and approximately 10 other full-time workers for housekeeping and landscaping. On October 22, 2019, lightning struck the mansion and started a fire while the property was unoccupied. The house and its contents were deemed a total loss, but nobody was injured.Why Chubb paid $8.75 million for the house but only $25,000 for its contentsPine Manor was insured under Chubb’s Masterpiece homeowner’s policy. Its Deluxe House section provided approximately $8.75 million in coverage for the building, while the Deluxe Contents section provided $3.5 million for personal property. The distinction between the two sections became central to the dispute. The building coverage did not contain the business-property exclusion at issue in the case, so Chubb paid the full $8.75 million policy limit for the mansion. The contents coverage, however, excluded losses involving business property, subject to an additional coverage provision that capped payment for such property at $25,000.The policy defined business property to include furniture, equipment, inventory, records and other items used to conduct the insured’s business. It covered activities intended to generate financial gain, whether conducted full time, part time or occasionally. Chubb argued that Gibson had used the contents of Pine Manor to operate his lodging and events business. The insurer therefore paid the $25,000 limit rather than the full $3.5 million contents amount.The dispute was not entirely unexpected. In June 2017, a Chubb underwriter had identified a potential gap in coverage after discovering that Pine Manor was no longer being used solely as a private residence. The underwriter warned Gibson’s insurance broker and recommended switching to commercial property insurance. Gibson nevertheless renewed the homeowner’s policy in 2018 and 2019. Gibson sued Chubb for breach of contract and alleged violations of the Illinois Insurance Code and the Illinois Consumer Fraud and Deceptive Business Practices Act. He sought the full contents coverage, arguing that the policy should not classify his personal furnishings and antiques as business property merely because the mansion hosted paying guests.What the Seventh Circuit decided in Gibson v. Chubb National Insurance CompanyThe district court ruled that most contents were subject to the $25,000 limit, except items in areas inaccessible to guests, including a wine cellar, a gun safe and 2 locked master-bedroom closets. The Seventh Circuit affirmed the district court’s decision in an opinion written by Judge Diane S. Sykes. It agreed that the policy’s definition of business property included furnishings and decorations used to conduct the lodging and events business, not just conventional office equipment. The court described the district judge’s interpretation as “exactly right,” concluding that the policy’s broad definition of business extended to property used in activities intended to generate financial gain. The court pointed to the role the mansion’s collection played in attracting guests and shaping their experience. Pine Manor’s website advertised its art and antiques as part of the estate’s appeal, and guests could access and use most of the furnishings and collections throughout the mansion. The court concluded that these items helped conduct the business. Gibson also argued that many items had been acquired before Pine Manor became a commercial venue and continued to serve personal purposes when his family visited. The court rejected that argument, explaining that the policy focused on how the contents were used when the loss occurred, not when or why they were purchased.The court also rejected Gibson’s argument that property qualified as business property only if it was used entirely for commercial purposes. It agreed with the district court that the policy covered property used “whether partially or fully” to conduct the business. The policy’s wording, including a provision addressing property used “in whole or in part” for business purposes, supported that interpretation. The court left open the narrower question of whether de minimis, or negligible, business use would be enough to trigger the exclusion. It did not decide that every instance of occasional business use automatically makes personal property ineligible for broader coverage. The Seventh Circuit affirmed summary judgment for Chubb on Gibson’s statutory claims under the Illinois Insurance Code and the Illinois Consumer Fraud and Deceptive Business Practices Act. The claim under Section 155 of the Illinois Insurance Code failed because a genuine dispute over coverage existed and Chubb had conducted a reasonable investigation. The Consumer Fraud Act claim also failed because Chubb’s coverage decision followed the policy’s plain terms. The court described the dispute as “not just genuine; it was justified” and said the district judge’s interpretation of the policy was “exactly right.”You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: No EC nod needed for voter to sue candidate over false information: Supreme Court
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: A voter can now not only cast a vote in an election but can also drag an election candidate to court and initiate criminal proceedings for
articles.body: NEW DELHI: A voter can now not only cast a vote in an election but can also drag an election candidate to court and initiate criminal proceedings for lying and furnishing a false declaration as Supreme Court has ruled that a complaint filed by a private person alleging an offence under Section 125-A of Representation of People Act (filing false affidavit) is maintainable and the Election Commission’s nod was not needed.Explaining the interplay between Section 125-A of Representation of People Act and Section 195(1) of the CrPC which says that no court shall take cognisance of any offences punishable under sections 172 to 188, including the offence of furnishing false information to a public servant, the top court held that Section 125A of RoP Act does not come within the ambit of Section 195 of CrPC and a court can take cognisance of a private complaint. The court’s ruling will further empower the electorate against candidates who lied in their affidavits.A bench of Justices Dipankar Datta and Sheel Nagu quashed the Karnataka HC order which had held that “right given to the voter is only to file an election petition, and not to register a private complaint of crime which is the duty of the Election Commission, if it wants to do so”.SC said that Section 125-A was inserted in the RoP Act in 2002, while Section 195 of CrPC was amended in 2006, and that the omission of the legislature to include Section 125-A of the RoP Act in Section 195 of CrPC was deliberate and no court would be barred from taking cognisance of an alleged offence under Section 125-A of the RoP Act, even on the complaint lodged by a private person.“Should we read into Section 195 of CrPC a prohibition in respect of Section 125-A of the RoP Act also, apart from those expressly included? If indeed it were the intention of the legislature that cognisance of any offence relating to furnishing of false information by a candidate in an affidavit with intent of being elected in an election (referred to in Section 125-A of the RoP Act) could only be taken if the complainant were a public servant, the same could have been provided by an amendment of Section 195, CrPC since Section 125-A of the RoP Act is of fairly recent origin.”SC also refused to give credence to the EC’s press note that it can take cognisance of such complaints and refer such matters to the relevant investigating authorities on a case-to-case basis. “...Even though the ECI is supreme in its own sphere and has, indeed, issued guidelines/press notes based on its understanding of the statutory provisions, interpretation of statutes is primarily the task of the courts and such guidelines/press notes do not bind us,” the court said.It said that Karnataka HC erred in holding that a private complaint cannot be filed for an offence under Section 125A of RoP Act which is punishable up to six months of jail term. The HC had interpreted the provision solely upon reading the letter issued by the Election Commission of India on the issue which was rejected by the apex court.Allaying the apprehension that allowing the lodging of a criminal complaint by a private person would be misused and frivolous cases would be filed by political rivals, SC said, “If at all a complaint is lodged to harass an elected candidate or frivolous allegations are levelled therein, the laws of the country duly empower the competent magistrates to pass such order(s) as they deem fit and proper commensurate with the facts and circumstances of each case.”Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: Interview | ‘AAP had 4.5 years to end drug menace, gangsterism in Punjab’: Sachin Pilot
articles.summary: Drug menace and underworld-crime are top issues in the upcoming elections in Punjab.
articles.body: Drug menace and underworld-crime are top issues in the upcoming elections in Punjab. AAP has shown no will to root them out, says Congress, but if voted to office, it will finish these off, AICC state in-charge Sachin Pilottells Subodh Ghildiyal. Excerpts:Where does Congress think the AAP govt has failed in Punjab?■ The top issue is the menace of drugs. The mafia and bureaucratic nexus is so overwhelming that home delivery of drugs is much quicker than home delivery of food. It’s ‘chitta’. As per NCRB 2024, Punjab had the second highest NDPS Act crime rate at 29 cases per lakh. If AAP govt had the will to finish off the drug menace, it would have done so in 4.5 years. Look at gangsterism, the nexus between people in jail and those operating outside carrying out shootouts, robberies. This had never been the culture of Punjab, even in its darkest hour. You never had homegrown gangs operating in public. Narco money feeds gang operations. Police/intelligence do not have the integrity and the political direction to curb this menace. These twin evils lead to unemployment. In Punjab, there are record Dalit atrocities, unemployment and persistent agrarian crisis. The AAP failure is taking the state downhill.Congress made you in-charge of Punjab in the context of infighting in the state unit with elections just five months away. And then it also changed its state chief Amrinder Singh Raja Warring.■Punjab is an important state not just for Congress, but also for the country. Its contribution — historical, political, social — is there for all to see. We are confident that the people of Punjab are looking for a change and Congress will provide that change. There may be different viewpoints, but there are no factions in the Punjab Congress. We are fighting unitedly to oust the AAP govt. Changes in the organisation are routine exercises.BJP is also slamming the AAP govt over drug menace.■Punjab is a border state and all the drugs are coming from across the border which is the responsibility of the Union ministry of home affairs and the defence ministry. So, it is wholly farcical when BJP launches an anti-drug drive in Punjab. What have they done to curb the menace on the borders of Rajasthan, Punjab and Gujarat. Mundra Port recorded the highest seizure of cocaine in history — Rs 21,000 crore in one consignment in 2021. Imagine how much cocaine would have slipped through unnoticed. BJP has to answer these questions.It will be a four-cornered contest between AAP, Congress, BJP and SAD.■The main contest is between AAP and Congress. Of the 13 Lok Sabha seats in 2024 polls, Congress won seven. BJP has no strong footing in Punjab and has survived on the back of SAD support. But SAD has also split and is facing internal issues. It is not the force like they were under Badal Senior. It will be a bipolar contest over who can lead Punjab better. There will be other players like Amritpal Singh’s party, but people of Punjab don’t give a fractured mandate. Congress played the role of a strong opposition for 4.5 years while others were missing. When in office, Congress has delivered in the past.Will Congress project a CM face in Punjab?■ Congress has never given the CM faces. There is a state president, campaign committee chairman, a legislature party leader — a whole lot of people who fight as a team.Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.body: NEW DELHI: Delhi’s Chamber of Trade and Industry (CTI) has urged LoP Rahul Gandhi to postpone Congress’s Nov 1 rally at Ramlila Maidan until after Nov 10, citing business disruptions during the peak Diwali shopping season. CTI said the rally could affect market access and traffic for three to four days, potentially impacting Rs 10,000 crore in festive trade.CTI chairman Brijesh Goyal said Delhi records Rs 25,000 crore in business on Dhanteras across major sectors. CTI claimed that traders suffered losses of Rs 3,000 crore in Oct due to rallies and road closures in Connaught Place, India Gate and central Delhi.CEC’s ‘impeachment’ on Oct 30INDIA bloc leaders will hold a “public impeachment” of CEC Gyanesh Kumar on Oct 30 and announce a public verdict. The “mock Parliament” will be held at Hotel Ashok, where top opposition netas would be present.Nov 1 rally by Rahul to hurt Sikhs: BJPCongress will be rubbing salt into the wounds of Sikhs by holding an Opposition rally on Nov 1, BJP said Saturday, alleging that the party had started anti-Sikh riots in “collusion” with its then govt on this very day in 1984.BJP claimed some Congress allies have disagreed with Rahul Gandhi’s decision to hold the rally on Nov 1, and said he will be not only hurting the sentiments of Sikhs but also inflicting huge losses on traders as the public meeting will be held during the festive period.“Rahul is irresponsible and indifferent to people’s plight. articles.title: A Baltimore house bought for $43,000 in 2022 was resold for $310,000 in 2023; three years later it was listed for $35,000 after foreclosure as lenders alleged a wider property fraud scheme involving hundreds of homes
articles.summary: A Baltimore property that changed hands for $43,000 in 2022 and was resold for $310,000 the following year returned to the market in 2026 for just $35,000
articles.body: A Baltimore property that changed hands for $43,000 in 2022 and was resold for $310,000 the following year returned to the market in 2026 for just $35,000 after foreclosure, becoming a striking example of an alleged real estate fraud scheme that has drawn scrutiny from lenders and investigators. In a report published by Realtor dot com on October 20, 2026, journalist Julie Gerstein detailed how two federal lawsuits accuse New York real estate investors Eluzer Gold and Benjamin Eidlisz, along with alleged associates, of inflating property values and securing loans against homes that were subsequently abandoned to foreclosure. The allegations have also featured in reporting by The Baltimore Banner, which investigated the investors’ property acquisitions in the city.How the Baltimore property changed handsThe house at 1829 N. Bond Street illustrates the transactions described in the lenders’ complaints. According to the lawsuits, Eidlisz bought the property for $43,000 in May 2022 before selling it in July 2023 to Levy Ventures, a limited liability company linked to Gold, for $310,000.The sharp increase in price allegedly occurred without the renovations that might have justified the higher valuation. The property later went into foreclosure and was listed for $35,000 in August 2026, according to Realtor dot com’s account of the legal filings.The transactions form part of broader allegations involving dozens of properties in Baltimore. Two lenders claim that the investors used companies they controlled to buy distressed homes, transfer them between related entities at substantially higher prices and obtain financing based on allegedly inflated appraisals. Many of the properties subsequently defaulted on their mortgages.Lenders allege a wider mortgage fraud schemeAmeritrust Mortgage Corporation filed a federal lawsuit in Maryland on September 9, alleging that Gold, Eidlisz and Shraga Chaim Lerner orchestrated a scheme involving 90 loans worth more than $14 million. The complaint alleges that the loans were obtained with the intention of defaulting on them while retaining the proceeds.A separate lawsuit filed a week later by RCN Capital and Commercial Lender alleges losses of another $10 million involving 59 properties purchased and subsequently defaulted upon between 2023 and 2024. Together, the complaints cover approximately 150 properties, a fraction of the roughly 700 homes the investors were reported to have acquired across the Baltimore area.According to the lenders, shell companies were used to facilitate rapid property transfers, while appraisals allegedly overstated values through inaccurate descriptions, manipulated photographs and other misrepresentations. The complaints contend that lenders would not have approved the financing had the properties been accurately valued. These remain civil allegations, and the lawsuits do not by themselves establish that every named defendant committed fraud.The role of investor property loansThe complaints also draw attention to debt service coverage ratio (DSCR) loans, a financing product commonly used by real estate investors. These loans generally assess a property’s ability to generate sufficient rental income to cover its debt payments, rather than relying primarily on the borrower’s personal income. Such financing can help investors acquire rental properties, but the lawsuits raise questions about the safeguards in place when properties are transferred between related companies and valuations rise sharply over short periods.The alleged scheme depended, in part, on lenders assessing individual transactions without necessarily seeing the full picture of an investor’s holdings and borrowing across multiple entities. If property values were artificially inflated, that could expose lenders to losses when borrowers stopped making payments and the homes entered foreclosure.Baltimore’s housing market faces the falloutThe allegations have emerged against the backdrop of Baltimore’s longstanding problems with vacant properties, deteriorating housing and housing insecurity. The city’s stock of historic row houses includes many distressed homes, particularly in neighbourhoods where residents have fewer financial resources to absorb sudden disruptions.Foreclosures can have consequences beyond the lenders and property owners involved. Tenants may face uncertainty about their housing, while neglected homes can affect neighbouring properties and complicate efforts to attract legitimate investment for rehabilitation. The Baltimore Banner’s earlier reporting brought attention to the investors’ extensive property acquisitions. An FBI investigation had been reported by The Baltimore Banner, although the FBI declined to confirm or deny its existence when approached by Realtor dot com.The case is not the only example of alleged property-value manipulation in Baltimore. A separate case involving investor Alexander Schultz and attorney Jacob Rappaport resulted in prison sentences earlier in 2026 over a similar scheme involving dozens of homes, according to Realtor dot com. For now, the lawsuits against Gold, Eidlisz and their alleged associates remain part of an ongoing legal process. The $35,000 listing of the Bond Street property offers a visible illustration of the gap between its reported purchase prices and its later market return, while the broader allegations raise questions about property valuations, investor lending and the costs of foreclosure in a city already struggling with distressed housing.You use AI every day. articles.title: Rs 10 lakh cover for 45 paise: Counter rail ticket buyers get insurance option
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: From Tuesday (Oct 27), all railway passengers buying reserved tickets from reservation counters can opt for travel insurance.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: From Tuesday (Oct 27), all railway passengers buying reserved tickets from reservation counters can opt for travel insurance. At present, optional travel insurance facility is available only for reserved tickets bought online.The insurance premium is only 45 paise per passenger, including taxes, with coverage of Rs 10 lakh in case of death and permanent total disability in a train accident.The scheme has provision for payment of Rs 7.5 lakh for permanent partial disability and up to Rs 2 lakh for hospitalisation expenses arising from injuries, as well as Rs 10,000 towards transportation of mortal remains of deceased passengers. The Railway Board has directed all its zones to implement the facility.It said, “Where a passenger opts for insurance, the applicable premium shall be collected along with the ticket fare through digital means only. Staff shall ensure that where the person is opting for insurance, payment is done through digital means.”Reservation staff will inform passengers about the availability of the optional insurance facility and facilitate the exercise of their choice.The board said reservation staff will ensure that the mobile number (mandatory) along with other requisite passenger particulars are captured accurately so as to facilitate transmission of relevant details to the insurance firm for issuance of the policy. Passengers opting for insurance shall be informed that the policy details will be communicated to their registered mobile number.It covers specified railway accidents and untoward incidents, including train collisions, derailments, violent attacks, robbery, arson and accidental falls from trains. Coverage extends to diverted routes and alternative transport arranged by the railways in certain cases of train diversion or short termination.Normal second class or general class passengers are not covered under the insurance policy. It is also not applicable to children below the age of 5 years for whom tickets are issued without a berth or seat. But it is applicable to children in 5-11 age group who have reservation with berth or without berth.Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.summary: Os candidatos Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) e Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) disputam neste domingo (25) quem será o próximo presidente do Brasil.
articles.body:
Os candidatos Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) e Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) disputam neste domingo (25) quem será o próximo presidente do Brasil.

Eleitores do estado de São Paulo retornam às urnas neste domingo (25) para definir quem será o próximo presidente do Brasil.

Quem não votou no primeiro turno pode votar neste domingo, se o título estiver em situação regular.

articles.title: In 2021, a Dallas home's flooring was damaged after a neighbour's frozen pipes burst; the insurer paid $4,261 but homeowners later sought $58,150 in repairs, and an October 22 court rejected the delayed claim
articles.summary: A federal appeals court has dismissed a lawsuit filed by Dallas homeowners who sought more than $58,000 for water damage.
articles.body: A federal appeals court has dismissed a lawsuit filed by Dallas homeowners who sought more than $58,000 for water damage. The court ruled that their legal action against State Farm was filed after the deadline set by their insurance policy had expired. The dispute began during severe weather in February 2021, when water pipes at a neighbouring property froze and burst. The resulting flood caused extensive damage to the floors and structure of the Dallas home. According to court documents published by the United States Court of Appeals for the Fifth Circuit on 22 October 2026, State Farm reviewed the initial claim and paid $4,261 (£3,280) in March 2021. At the time, the insurer told the homeowners they could submit additional receipts for replacement cost benefits as repairs continued. However, the homeowners waited until well after the two-year contractual deadline had passed before seeking another $58,150 in repair costs. This led to a legal dispute over insurance coverage and the deadline for filing a lawsuit.Court confirms strict deadline on insurance disputesThe Fifth Circuit panel upheld a lower federal district court's decision in favour of State Farm. It agreed that all claims linked to the 2021 winter freeze were filed too late under Texas law. Under the Texas Civil Practice and Remedies Code, parties to an insurance contract can agree to a shorter deadline for legal action, provided it is at least two years. State Farm's policy included a standard two-year limit, starting from the date the legal claim first arose. The three-judge panel explained that State Farm had made its position on the initial coverage decision clear on 12 March 2021, when it processed the first payment. The court stressed that Texas law does not require an insurer to use formal legal terms or specific wording to communicate a claim decision, as long as its position is clear. Because the homeowners did not file a lawsuit within two years of that March 2021 decision, the court ruled that their claims under the insurance contract and state law had expired.Rejection of bad faith and misrepresentation argumentsDuring the appeal, the homeowners argued that State Farm had not properly investigated the full extent of the water damage. They also claimed the insurer had misled them by inviting them to submit more receipts for repair work. The appeals court rejected these arguments. It explained that claims under Texas insurance law for breach of good faith and fair dealing must also be filed within two years of the date they arise. The court also said that letters or other communications inviting policyholders to submit additional repair receipts do not restart or extend the legal deadline. An extension can apply only if a formal waiver is established before the deadline expires. The panel concluded that routine letters allowing customers to provide further receipts cannot be used to bring separate fraud or misrepresentation claims to get around the usual time limits. The ruling also noted that the homeowners had declined Additional Living Expense (ALE) coverage for the 2021 incident. They chose to stay at a second property they owned while repairs were carried out on their Dallas home.Impact of consecutive winter stormsThe court filing also showed that the same Dallas property suffered further flooding during another major winter storm in Texas in December 2022. The storm caused additional internal water pipes to burst. The homeowners reported the 2022 damage to State Farm under a separate claim number. However, their later appeal focused only on the unresolved payment dispute linked to the 2021 storm. By upholding the lower court's decision, the Fifth Circuit found that State Farm had met its legal duties in handling the original 2021 claim. articles.title: 'You have shown us what hard work can achieve': Shikhar Dhawan lauds Indian para-athletes after record 114-medal haul
articles.summary: In a groundbreaking achievement, India's para-athletes clinched a historic 114 medals at the 2026 Asian Para Games with just 168 participants. Their impressi...
articles.body:
Former India opener Shikhar Dhawan lauded the country's para-athletes after they scripted history at the Asian Para Games 2026, returning with a record haul of 114 medals and securing their best-ever fourth-place finish in the continental event. India's para-athletes marched with the national flags at the closing ceremony at Paloma Mizuho Stadium on Friday, bringing the curtains down on a landmark campaign in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan. The contingent finished with 30 gold, 35 silver and 49 bronze medals, surpassing its previous best of 108 medals at the 2022 edition in Hangzhou. Congratulating the athletes on their achievement, Dhawan took to X and wrote: "A record 114 medals and India's best-ever fourth-place finish at the Asian Para Games! 🇮🇳 Congratulations to our para-athletes on a phenomenal campaign. You have shown us what dedication, belief and hard work can achieve. Champions! 🙌"

India surpass previous best despite smaller contingent

India's performance in Japan was particularly impressive given that the contingent comprised 168 para-athletes, significantly fewer than the 309 who represented the country in Hangzhou three years ago. Despite the smaller contingent, Indian athletes delivered outstanding performances across disciplines, including para-athletics, para-badminton, para-archery, para-shooting, table tennis and swimming. The 2026 medal tally improved on India's previous best at the 2022 Games, when the country initially won 111 medals before three were revoked following doping violations involving Neeraj Yadav and Parveen, leaving the final tally at 108 medals.

Mona Agarwal, Nishad Kumar lead Indian contingent at closing ceremony

Double gold medallist para-shooter Mona Agarwal and high-jumper Nishad Kumar carried the Indian flag as co-flag-bearers at Friday's closing ceremony, symbolising the country's memorable campaign.

articles.title: Trump votes in Florida midterms, defends controversial ad, doubles down on Iran war
articles.summary: US President Donald Trump voted in Florida’s midterm elections on Saturday, saying he had supported Republican candidates across the ballot before heading
articles.body: US President Donald Trump voted in Florida’s midterm elections on Saturday, saying he had supported Republican candidates across the ballot before heading to Georgia for a campaign rally.Trump and first lady Melania Trump arrived together at a polling station at the Palm Beach County Supervisor of Elections office in West Palm Beach. The president had spent the morning at a nearby golf course before casting his vote.Trump has previously faced criticism for voting by mail despite repeatedly attacking the practice. Asked whether he had voted for candidates from his own party, he replied, "Very much so."Trump defends controversial campaign adSpeaking to reporters after voting, Trump defended an advertisement by Ohio Republican gubernatorial candidate Vivek Ramaswamy that has drawn widespread criticism.The ad features the estranged mother of Ramaswamy’s Democratic rival, Dr Amy Acton. She lost custody of her children after her husband, the children's stepfather, was indicted for raping Acton when she was 12.Trump also defended his decision to direct his administration to file a lawsuit seeking to block certification of Alaska’s US Senate election if Republican Senator Dan Sullivan loses. The dispute centres on the presence of another candidate named Dan Sullivan on the ballot.Trump comments on Iran warAsked about the war in Iran, Trump said the United States could either continue its military campaign or reach an agreement with Tehran."I may have to finish it off. Or maybe they will make a deal, but I am not sure. Either way, we win."Melania Trump was also asked whether she might travel to Ukraine. Her comments came after she brokered a ceasefire between Russia and Ukraine in the devastated, Russian-occupied Ukrainian city of Oleshky this week to allow humanitarian aid deliveries and civilian evacuations."We will see," she told reporters.Trump backs Republicans in Florida racesIn Florida, Trump has endorsed Republican Representative Byron Donalds in the race to succeed Governor Ron DeSantis, who cannot seek another term because of term limits. Donalds is facing David Jolly, who has moved from the Republican Party to independent politics and later joined the Democratic Party.Trump has also campaigned for Republican Senator Ashley Moody, who is seeking election to the final two years of former Senator Marco Rubio’s term.
